_comment: Pricing & capability database for the MindRouter Cluster Configurator. Machine-refreshed (see tools/update-pricing.md). All prices USD street-price ranges [low, high], compiled from vendor/reseller listings via live web research. VRAM figures are weights-only unless noted. Perf figures are aggregate batched decode tok/s per GPU on vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM-class stacks at interactive SLAs (conservative ends of published benchmarks).
generated_by: Live web research: NVIDIA/Supermicro/Thinkmate/WiredZone/AVADirect/Exxact listings; InferenceMAX, MLPerf, LMSYS, DatabaseMart, CloudRift benchmarks; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (Jul 2026 snapshot) for model scores.

assumptions.quantization: Primary models served in NVFP4/MXFP4 (FP8 where VRAM allows); frontier models ship 4-bit-native
assumptions._power_note: Measured serving power: decode ~34-40% of TDP, saturated continuous batching 65-80%; ~50% is the configurator's nominal per user-facing assumption
assumptions._peak_note: Production LLM traces show ~3.3x diurnal peak-to-average (Azure trace); 4x is conservative

gb10.label: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)
gb10.notes: 128 GB unified LPDDR5X (273 GB/s), ~119 GB usable; 240 W nameplate system power, ~170 W measured under heavy AI load

rtx6000pro.label: RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell (Server) 96 GB
rtx6000pro.notes: GDDR7-shortage pricing (launched at $8,565; NVIDIA marketplace $13,250 Jul 2026). Passive server card, 400-600 W configurable

h200nvl.label: H200 NVL 141 GB
h200nvl.notes: PCIe dual-slot, HBM3e 4.8 TB/s; the 141 GB option for standard Supermicro PCIe chassis

b200.label: B200 SXM 180 GB
b200.notes: Shipping HGX B200 is 180 GB/GPU (1.4 TB per 8-GPU node); sold as systems, per-GPU price is OEM-quote derived

b300.label: B300 (Blackwell Ultra) SXM 288 GB
b300.notes: 288 GB HBM3e (~270 GB usable), 2.3 TB per 8-GPU node; ~1,100 W in HGX air-cooled configs (1,400 W in NVL72 liquid)

platforms.label: NVIDIA DGX Spark
platforms.notes: DGX Spark Founders $4,699 (MSRP raised +18% Feb 2026, DRAM shortage); partner GB10 boxes (MSI EdgeXpert, ASUS Ascent GX10) from ~$2,999. Two units pair over 200G ConnectX QSFP; 3+ units cluster via QSFP switch per NVIDIA's Spark Stacking playbooks

platforms.label: Supermicro 2U GPU server + RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell
platforms.notes: Barebone $4,760 (WiredZone Jul 2026); base price is configured without GPUs (1x Xeon 6700P, 512 GB DDR5, NVMe)

platforms.label: Supermicro 4U/5U GPU server + RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell
platforms.notes: Barebones $11.5k-$25k; base price is configured without GPUs (dual EPYC/Xeon, 768 GB-1.5 TB DDR5)

platforms.label: Supermicro HGX B200 8-GPU
platforms.notes: Full system with 8x B200 (1.4 TB HBM3e). Street $330k-$500k; DGX B200 anchors the floor at ~$280k-$320k. 8-16 wk lead times

platforms.label: Supermicro HGX B300 8-GPU (liquid-cooled)
platforms.notes: Quote-only; estimated from the verified air-cooled sibling. Requires rack CDU / facility water (not included)

platforms.label: Supermicro HGX B300 8-GPU (air-cooled)
platforms.notes: Verified configured quotes $420k (TurboMaxGPU) to $504k (AVADirect configurator); scalper ceilings to $760k excluded

models.label: Small (~4B)
models.notes: Best current ~4B-class model; multimodal. Score is a low-confidence estimate (no AA listing)

models.label: Compact (~20B MoE)
models.notes: Native MXFP4; unbeatable latency for the footprint

models.label: Fast MoE (~120B)
models.notes: Native MXFP4, sliding-window attention = tiny KV; batches extremely well. Newer small models score higher but this remains a throughput workhorse

models.label: Capable (~31B)
models.notes: Dense, multimodal (text/image/video), 256K context; most token-efficient of its class

models.label: Fast & capable (35B MoE)
models.notes: MoE ~3B active: throughput champion of the mid tier; multimodal

models.label: Sharp (27B dense)
models.notes: Best intelligence-per-GB in the open field (AA 37/57 vs frontier); dense so per-GPU throughput is lower than the MoE tiers; multimodal, hybrid linear attention keeps KV small

models.label: Near-frontier (~750B MoE)
models.notes: Highest-scoring downloadable open model (AA 51/57), MIT license, 1M context; 4-bit fits one 8-GPU node

models.label: Frontier (2.8T MoE)
models.notes: Open-weight frontier (AA 57.1, #3 overall, Jul 16 2026). Trained quantization-aware in MXFP4: ~1.4 TB weights is the native serving tier; needs an HGX B300-class node minimum

perf_tok_s_per_gpu._comment: Aggregate batched decode tok/s per GPU at interactive SLAs (conservative ends of InferenceMAX / MLPerf / LMSYS / DatabaseMart / CloudRift / dendro-logic published numbers). null = does not fit or not practical.

storage._storage_note: 2026 NAND crisis pricing: enterprise 15-30TB U.2/E1.S NVMe at ~$370-650/TB street, ~4x year-ago levels
